title: From a square or a street: -ról/-ről

sections.title: Places with -n
sections.content: You know the ending *-n/-on/-en* from days (*szombaton*). Some places use it for 'on' or 'at' instead of *-ban/-ben*: *a téren* (on the square), *a piacon* (at the market), *az utcán* (in the street). For 'from' these take *-ról/-ről*: *a térről*, *a piacról*, *az utcáról*. The question is the same: *Honnan jössz? A piacról jövök.* Back or front works as before (*piacról*, *térről*), and a final *-a* lengthens (*utcáról*). New words: *hegy* (hill) and *pálya* (pitch).

sections.title: Where, and from where
rows: on the square → from the square
at the market → from the market
in the street → from the street
on the hill → from the hill
on the pitch → from the pitch

sections.content: A place that is said with *-n/-on* never takes *-ból*: not *a térből*, but *a térről*.
